reviews.snippet: Baristas were super nice and helpful when I was trying to decide what to get. I ended up with a winter espresso with steamed oat milk for cortado. The atmosphere was relaxing and a perfect way to start my day. Love the signature blue bottle cup!
Decaf cappuccino is quite bitter. Price is way above nearby cafe. The atmosphere is nice though.

Delighted to be warmly greeted by the friendly Randy who is super knowledgeable about the menu at Blue Bottle—recommending the waffles and Hot Nola coffee which tasted awesome! He also introduced the newly launched instant espresso which is perfect as gifts—just in time for Christmas—since Blue Bottle isn't in my country. Love that I can bring the taste back home to my friends!

This outlet has a light and airy ambience with outdoor seats to enjoy the sights of a lovely neighborhood. It's also a short walk from Colombia University which makes it a nice stop to grab coffee before visiting the campus.

I love the soft arabica brand coffee they using to make cappuccino. It's may be little expensive, compare to other coffee places, but It worth every penny.
It's very roomy inside, but I prefer seat outside (if weather permit) and observe crazy, dynamic live of this beautiful city with cup of lovely coffee.

The coffee is pretty good, mostly, besides the fact they serve you iced coffee in a paper cup with no straw. I think its time to go back to plastic for this type of drink. They are super expensive, always were. The space inside is ok, not a great vibe and you can sit outside as well. Not a.lot of options in that area.

Sue & Abby stole the show!!

This is a hidden gem of a spot in new york city especially if you are in the Morningside Heights area and love coffee, awesome service and super chill ambiance — Blue Bottle is a must.

This coffee spot has a truly chic atmosphere — modern seating, sleek tables, and warm, inviting lighting that gives the place a cozy yet upscale feel. The vibe is stylish without being pretentious, and the staff are friendly and attentive, adding to the welcoming energy. It’s the kind of place you’ll want to linger in with a latte and good company.

Will definitely return!

P.S. - check out the pic of this awesome Cherry Blossom Latte!! It was totally deelish! 😋☕️🍒

If you go to school at columbia university or in need of excellent coffee, you need to come to this blue bottle location.

Their staff are extremely knowledgeable and create great coffee.

Please note that they make REAL coffee (NOT coffee flavoured beverages).

Both Ryan and Randy created my order (Perfect flat white) using single origin coffee.

The place is spotless, kind and most importantly they know their ****

Enjoy your coffee!

Such a cute coffee spot! The coffee is really good, and I love that their oat milk is gluten-free — a small detail that makes a big difference for me. I just wish they had some gluten-free pastries too!

The quality and consistency of their lattes are too dependent on the barrista, which is unfortunate given the price. 50/50 so far in receiving a warm cup of milk vs a latte where you can actually taste the coffee

Fellow Aussies are all over NYC coffee like flies to roadkill. But not all Aussie cafes are true blue. This is as NYC as a Cafe gets. From the pretentious uncaring welcome, the equally pretentious airport minimalist ambience, while 80s rock blasts incongruously, the mediocre coffee that's been fussed over like its the birth of the last koala on the planet, to being (literally) yelled at to come back into the almost empty shop to return my cups to the DIY bussing area...how very NYC...and all after paying $12 for the 2 coffee pleasure. Nyc is full of genuinely Aussie cafes serving great food and coffee (citizens of Chelsea/Bleeker, blank street for example). These owners may have the passport, but they've acclimatised unhealthily.
The staff is really friendly and the matcha is consistently excellent. Sometimes they will do fun laté art. Around Christmas the barista drew a grinch in my matcha it was adorable 😍

Ordered regular drip coffee (small - brown cup on the picture ), and iced!!! Coffee- on the right - medium!!!) came up to 12$ and change! When I inquired the person at the counter why my small coffee and medium size coffee are the same size - he answered : “oh there is actually a difference”. Also Iced coffee came with weird foam? When again inquired where the thick foam on my iced coffee (not latte) came from - the answer was - that when you shake the milk the foam comes. Never ever coming back! Horrible ! Rip off
Clean atmosphere. I've had a costa rica blend in Chicago that was really good. The Burundi one they had here was not to my taste. But I'm sure if I went another day, it would be better.
The coffee is good. The staff is quite friendly. Above all, the atmosphere is different and well suited for work or hanging out with a friend.

Coffee was clearly over priced, not to mention the terrible attitude of the white male barista with curly hair. He took my order multiple times and never paired attention to my words. He replied in sarcastic tone like I never could afford such pricy coffee. He mistaken my name into a completely different name. When they finally realized they messed up with the names, the coffee has been sit there for a while and was watery.

Great experience here. Joseph was friendly, fast, and knowledgeable about the menu and drinks, and very patient am with my questions. The cafe was very clean and had good music playing, and my drink was amazing! They did seem a little understaffed but there was no line while I was here so I guess I got lucky.

Very neat place for a coffee chat.
I went there to have a chat and enjoyed it.
It smells delicious coffee and the hot chocolate was good but nothing extraordinary either.

The idea is that they provide above average coffee, which may be true, but the experience here isn’t good at all. Cashier guy looked pissed that I wanted to order coffee. I tipped him, not sure why… also looked unhappy about that. While I sat and tried to enjoy the coffee there was so much gossip and conversation from the staff, it was impossible to enjoy the experience. So, I highly recommend Nussbaum & Wu, star bucks or the new Turkish place. But not this location

To whom it may concern. I had a hot NOLA I. Several of your stores for $ 5.65 + TAX. Today I asked at this store and a not so welcoming Asian male employee tried to charge me $ 6.00 + tax. NO WAY!! I’m not paying this store increase because their rent is high or because they have to pay more electricity due to A/C. Be respectful with your customers.
Good matcha. Not sure about the coffee but was packed when I came. There's also some construction going on around the building.

Best espresso in town. Want a really good espresso come here. And it helped that most of the employees in here are very friendly. There are couple that looks like they were forced to work by the majority are really nice people

While it has become standard to wait for one’s coffee in coffee shops in New York City for anywhere between 15 and 30 minutes, even when it seems like there is no one in front of you in line, my wait for my drink this morning at this place was pretty epic.

But even more delightful than the absurd wait time for my drink was the sarcastic mockery with which I was met when my drink was put in my hand.

I had ordered a hot chocolate “extra extra hot.” Most of us who are New Yorkers know that there’s a tendency to make hot chocolates room temperature in this city. So my hack is to just order it “extra extra hot”. But the young person who was standing next to the young person who actually made my drink felt it necessary to say in a very mocking tone “but it’s like really extra extra extra hot” and roll their eyes after the person who actually made my drink handed it to me. They were not even clever enough to make fun of me, and mock me, after I had walked away.

As someone who grew up working in the service industry and who even worked as a bartender and a waitress in New York City when I was in school, I understand the urge to mock customers. Fair game. But one would think you would be mindful enough to wait until they can’t hear you.

Overall, my experience was about a three. The hot chocolate was pretty delicious. The young person who actually took my order initially was wonderful. But the end of the line in the coffee production at the place is a mess.

If this had been a hot chocolate that cost three dollars I probably would’ve rolled with it but this was, you see, the six dollar variety of hot chocolate. So unless you’re up for six dollar hot chocolate and snide, mocking teenagers, perhaps give it a pass.
Really cold all the time, even in the winter. Not a great place to do work and the coffee is not great.

I've been to a few Blue Bottle cafes and the one in the Walker Hotel is especially nice. I had one of their seasonal NOLA iced coffees and it was perfect. Coffee quality is consistently top notch and reflected in the price. More expensive, yet much better than any Starbucks. I mainly make coffee at home and their beans are always fresh. Any of the bags you buy in the cafe will have been roasted within the past two weeks.
Always love blue bottle coffees, I’d choose them whenever I see them. Light but flavorful.
Best espresso in NYC. Expensive, but worth it. Have it there and it's served with a small glass of San Pelegrino. Just like Trieste. Sort of.
the best latte i have ever had (latte with whole milk) — Hayes valley espresso
Good in general, good location, somehow best coffee near Columbia U.
Love the coffee, but the service is hit-or-miss. One barista was clearly frazzled, and yesterday the wait was long with staff seemingly preoccupied. My coworker even noticed the stressed vibe.

They need to work on their pour over. I'm happy to pay $5 plus tax and tip for a good pour over, but it's not very good. The roast tastes burnt. Perhaps it's because they're using a "winter blend", which tends to be a blend of cheaper, dark roasted beans. Atmosphere: blond wood everything and a Columbia crowd that wears a lot of black. Wifi is good.

Coffee is great but today’s service was poor - ordered a breakfast item - the person at the checkout counter missed it , when I reminded him , he wasn’t sorry at all for missing the order - actually was offended I pointed it out

Coffee was amazing !

Blue Bottle Coffee might be one of the most elegant cafes that has reasonable prices. They will brew your coffee before your eyes by the cup( it takes about 3 minutes) and you know it’s fresh and, yes, delicious! I had a perfectly balanced and delicious almond latte.

After a run, my friend and I decided to get some coffee and chai. My friend wanted the coffee, but Blue Bottle didn't have honey or cinnamon as condiments. For such a high end coffee shop, they should have those things. My chai was full of foam. The customer service was trash, especially from the cashier. He looked like he hated life.
Well, tried it, won't be going back

The pour-over coffee is quite decent, albeit expensive at $5 a 12oz cup. I don't go here often because of the price, just when I don't have the chance to brew my own. The staff members are polite, and the ambiance isn't hectic, loud, or crowded.
Just got a coffee to go, but it was a smooth flavor and decently quick service for NYC. looking forward to checking them out again next time I am near the Strategist.

People who work here are very unfriendly. I was charged $7 for a cup of coffee. Cold milk was added which made the coffee to get cold. People working there were not able to steam or microwave my coffee and did not even offer a replacement. Bunch of dudes who don't know what they are doing work here and absolutely have no customer service skills whatsoever. Go for other coffee shops.

I used to love blue bottle coffee. Especially thier NOLA ice coffee. But ice coffee should come in a see through cup, and now have been serving it in a hot coffee paper cup for a few years. There are conpostable see through cups if you care about the environment. If you want to charge $6, you should provide the full experience.

At this specific location its also very difficult to find a spot to sit down as students come in with their laptops and spend hours.

Their hot chocolate is surprisingly good.

Blue bottle has been one of my favorite, but my last experience was disappointing. I think the barista poured some pre-made espresso from a cup and then went on steaming the milk to make my latte. I understand it as a way of saving time especially during rush time; however, the quality of coffee would be affected and even if there are customers who don’t care, those who can tell the difference would be very disappointed.

Good vibes and I’ve always had great interactions with the people who work there! A particular shoutout to Kayla— she helped me get an approximate spiced drink when the one I was gonna buy had caffeine and I was going for decaf. 5 stars to the people there ⭐️

Got an iced coffee, plain, nothing added, and it was 7 dollars. Seven. Dollars. It was a good cup of coffee, the employees were nice, but I probably won’t come back here because of the price. The menu board also didn’t have the price listed, which I feel like is kind of a scam. Overall good coffee but way way way overpriced.

$5 for a small cup of regular coffee. And was barely warm. You had one job…

P.S.: minimum tip is 15% - you would think with their prices and minimal service they could pay their workers a decent enough salary?

The baristas got me here. For the whole month of April, you get 50 cents off when you bring your own cup.

I usually order the iced oat milk nola. For vegan food I sometimes get the banana bread, which tastes like cake, the chia seed and orange cup, occasionally pairing it with one of their small pieces of dark chocolate. The overnight oat cup is also vegan.

Three stars because the prices are obscenely high, even for Manhattan. However, if you have a lot of disposable income and paying $7+ for a 12oz iced coffee doesn't phase you, absolutely try it. The coffee was very good as was the service. Much better than SBUX.

Want to order and sit in for 15 mins there while the baristas serve 20 online pickup orders before you get your coffee? Me neither. Just straight lack of respect.

Pretty good coffee but expensive, & food is good, hence 3 star
admittedly the coffee is pretty good, but regardless of when you go expect to wait a minimum of 10 minutes for your order and horrible attitude from the baristas like no other
Beautiful place, an ambience set for working peacefully, helpful staff and great coffee! Loved their Shakerato.

Why do people come here?

Don't waste your time or money. The product is no way near worth the cost.

1. Coffee is NOT significantly better than other places.
2. Coffee takes WAY longer and not hot enough.
3. PRICES are really really high. Absurdly so.
4. It's a corporate chain.
5. Staff were ok. Working a public facing service job is hard.

I am standing in “line” - waiting patiently- when I arrive the man is talking to this person - after several minutes I raise my hand . He telsl ME one moment - not the person he’s talking with (who has already ordered and what not) and I wait a second or two and notice he’s not finishing his convo. And I walk away without saying anything not a peep- as I’m walking away he says: “you should practice patience” - I was like are you out of your mind!! With that said - I am certain blue bottle is going under. The audacity of that man? .
Lots of computer people working hard and selflessly taking up all the seats, but the coffee is really good.
Love Blue Bottle and love this location in particular. All the baristas here are really sweet and the coffee is always fantastic, as to be expected from Blue Bottle. By far my favorite coffee chain.

Good place with wrong people :)
Gave me a haunted snow man!

Every time I come here, by far the worst service of any of the Blue Bottle in NYC. Everyone has an attitude in this place, staff here needs to undergo some customer service training. Definitely not what you expect from a Blue Bottle. I’ll stick to the midtown locations from now on.

Overpriced but excellent coffee. The barista rudely directed me away from the small opening in the plexiglass through which he talked to me. Note that I was the only masked customer ("guest") in the whole store. The remaining 28 guests were unmasked.
Barristas: please stop confusing cortados with lattes/cappuccinos! See photo: ordered cortado.
I had a cappuccino. Maybe the best steam milk I’ve ever had. Made by Santos . The coffee was grade too. Really good.
My favorite drink at Blue Bottle is the New Orleans iced coffee. While on the pricier side, Blue Bottle offers some of the best coffee among widely available coffeeshop chains

Great atmosphere and the place is definitely beautiful.

They are pretty slow, it takes a few minutes just to get a cup of coffee.

The coffee itself is OKish and it is pretty expensive.
The barista was so friendly; after a long work day his kindness made my day! My drink was great, but I will be back for the amazing service.

The food was NOT worth the price. I got a tiny sandwich for $8!!! The atmosphere was mediocre. The ambience was basic, the coffee and food is overpriced and underwhelming. Save yourself the disappointment adlnd go to a different and better Cafe.
Spoke with Rex, the manager, regarding an issue last week. Resolved and a cup of latte with almond milk on the House. Beautiful. New to the neighborhood, but everytime I pass by, ..its full.

Either your staff needs more training of how to cook rice noodles properly, or your recipe and SOP (if they exist at all) need to change.

Staff is good, they tried to be helpful, but unfortunately the noodles tasted the same. Beef is great though.

I came around lunch time and the line wrapped around the customers eating their meals making it odd to pass by. I noticed the menu trays were empty, so I had limited time to pick. There are additional offerings by the counter that were not on the sign.
The beef soup bowl was nice in itself - the beef was ample and very tender. The soup was a bit salty and oily, but easy to drink. The noodles were decent and a bit mushy - there didn't seem to be a way to swap it out when ordering.
The venue was fairly quiet and well lit. When I ordered in, I had the bowl by itself (without cover), so be careful when carrying it as the soup is fairly hot

reviews.snippet:
We ordered delivery and everything arrived well-packed and still comforting and flavorful. Highlights included the steamed pork soup dumplings (xiao long bao)—juicy, delicate skins, and especially good with the dumpling soy sauce and chili oil. The classic chicken broth was clean and soothing, perfect as a warm add-on, and the smashed cucumber salad was crisp and refreshing, balancing the richer dishes nicely.

The standout for our family was the classic chicken noodle soup with wide knife noodles and chili oil on the side—deep, satisfying broth and chewy noodles that held up well in delivery. We also loved the tomato egg noodles with slow-braised pork, which were savory, comforting, and generously portioned. Our seven-year-old devoured the noodles and braised pork, which is always the ultimate seal of approval.

Overall: reliable, flavorful Chinese comfort food that travels well and pleases both adults and kids. We’ll definitely order again.

response.snippet:
Dear Anna,

Feedback like this really warms our heart, we try to provide the best experience for our customers as we improve our business. We will continue working on making the most quality products available for you. We hope to serve you again soon in the future!

reviews.snippet: This taste like shit, I want to pick up one from the grill, but server grabbed one from the box instead and said “Same thing🤣”. It is worst sausage I have ever tried burned, stale and literally rock-hard. It spends me 27 dollars.

reviews.snippet: I had lunch at this Asian bowl spot. The decor is nice and simple, modern looking. The counter is well layed out with each step explained. There are a lot of options from salad bowls, to rice bowls, and noodle bowls. There's also a good variety of base sauce options. I ordered the flat noodles with tomato egg sauce. I also got the chili oil as a garnish which added some kick to the dish. The service was fast and great, prices were reasonable. Food tasted good overall.

Instant favorite! Junzi does not use any nuts in their kitchen and they have many items without sesame, which is labeled on their menu. I was able to have Chinese food for the first time in years without my allergies flaring up. So far I’ve tried the Tomato Egg Noodles with Slow-Braised Pork (pictured) and a similar bowl with the Shanghai Scallion sauce and chili oil (which I liked even more). The steamed vegetable dumplings are also delicious. The folks working there are super nice too. So glad to have this gem in my neighborhood.

response.snippet: Hello Nicole. Thank you for this wonderful review. We are really happy that your experience with Junzi was an excellent one! This is making us more motivated to improve on the way to our future goals! We look forward to serving you again soon!

reviews.snippet: super yummy! pork wonton soup was filling and soo yummy, the epitome of umami. and the beef noodle soup was great, just wish i opted for different noodles. some noodle soups are a bit pricey, but if im ever super hungry i can grab the pork wontons. my new go-to spot!

It means a lot to hear we’ve become your new go-to spot, and we look forward to serving you again the next time you’re craving wontons!

reviews.snippet: The food was simply not good. I was not impressed. I ordered the braised(5hours)beef bowl with noodles and it wasn’t that amazing. The noodles themself were alright and the vegetables fine as well. Nothing special wouldn’t recommend. The lady that met us at the register was really friendly and nice though.

reviews.snippet: Just visited Junzi Kitchen and it’s a fantastic spot for anyone who loves customizable Chinese cuisine. The dim sum, like the Steamed Chicken & Shrimp Shumai and Boiled Pork Wontons, was delicious and perfectly paired with soy dipping sauce. But the standout was definitely the “Build Your Own” option. I went with Tomato Egg Noodles with Slow-braised Pork and was blown away by the rich, flavorful tomato egg sauce. The Lion’s Head Meatballs and Shanghai Scallion Noodles were equally impressive, each dish bursting with authentic flavors. Junzi Kitchen offers a unique way to enjoy classic dishes your way. Highly recommend for a fresh take on Chinese favorites!

New Asian version of chipotle where you build your own noodles or wrap. The ingredients are fresh and sauces are tasty. The noodles are freshly blanched in front of you and is served dry. The place is clean and staff are friendly. Price was a little bit more than expected for a self service place. Overall, pleasant experience.

SO delicious. The restaurant is a Chipotle-style take on Chinese food - but make no mistake, it’s fresh and not oily/greasy at all. It feels as authentic as it gets here in the US, and the dishes are loaded with tons of fresh veggies. Definitely recommend, especially on a cold day!

Rainy NYC day cravings led me to this cozy gem near Columbia University. The spring noodles with sour & spicy sauce + mapo tofu hit the spot.
Warm vibes, great staff. A must visit if you're in the Manhattan area. 🍜🌧️🔥

The staff were also so kind. They ran out of scallions for my order and I was okay going without but right before I finished paying someone got me some freshly cut scallions. reviews.snippet:
Suspected MSG use.

Had their beef noodle soup. The taste was normal to below average. I came here twice and both times after having their chicken and beef soup options, developed dizziness and headache within 15 minutes of the meal. I suspect they put MSG in their dishes. While MSG is not illegal, many people are sensitive to it and may feel uncomfortable after consumption.

If you know you are sensitive to MSG, avoid this restaurant at all costs.

Junzi has become the spot for me and my friends. The food is always fresh, filling, and full of flavor—especially the Mapo Tofu Bowl with either the rice noodles or brown rice (my ultimate comfort order).

But what really sets Junzi apart is the team. Terry, David, Angel, Yami, and Denise are just the best, so warm, welcoming, and genuinely fun to be around.

It’s rare to find a place where the food hits and the people feel like friends.
Always a go to!

Junzi Kitchen is an absolute gem! We tried the soup dumplings, pork chive dumplings, and the slow braised beef noodle soup, and every bite was exceptional. The soup dumplings were perfectly crafted, with a delicious, savory broth that burst with flavor. The pork chive dumplings had a delightful balance of freshness and richness, and the slow braised beef noodle soup was simply divine—tender beef, rich broth, and perfectly cooked noodles.

Calm atmosphere, the service was quick and friendly, and the quality of the food truly sets Junzi Kitchen apart. Whether you're looking for a quick bite or a satisfying meal, this is the place to go. Highly recommend!

Although they were good, I don't think they paired well with the rest of the ingredients that I chose. This is a good spot if you're ever around the area and in need of a quick meal.

First time here. This a build your own noodle bowl 🍜chinese restaurant. First pick noodle bowl or bing (like a tortilla/wrap). Then pick ur noodle 🍝(spaghetti or flat noodle). Then pick your ingredients. I choose the 🍅 tomato pork 🐷bowl. It included tomato sauce, cilantro, pickled carrots and daikon, and cooked pork. The shredded pork 🐖was so good. It had that roasted flavor to it. The tomato sauce was too sweet🍯 to be honest though. Beverages here are teas🌿 on tap and niche sodas and asian label boxed fruit 🍏🍐🍈 juices.
I had the dumplings here for a little over $10 with tax. The portion is generous I could eat it for two meals. I also love the soup with shellfish.

reviews.snippet:
I was on my way to Milano market to have a cheeky gluten & dairy cheat day when the sign for this caught my eye. So, all, i sacrificed my lunch for this review.

I got the beef bone broth soup with rice noodles to-go because the ambience is not great— corporate bowl feel, which is ok.

The beef in the soup is great, exactly what i expected. The soup itself, not so much. Does not have the depth of flavor i’d expect from something simmered for 5 hours. Also lacking in salt— and more than in a health-conscious way. Perhaps i should have added a hoisin sauce— although the soup should stand alone well i think. Also also, they gave me normal noodle not rice >:(

Overall, would not go again, i can make this menu myself and better.

Good selection of food. I would come back here to try some other menu.

reviews.snippet: Extremely positive experience here! Super friendly team and DELICIOUS NOODLES!!!!! If you want a casual and TASTY and HEALTHY (so many greens!!!) bowl of happiness , i strongly recommend junzi! And they were so patient with all my menu questions when it was my first time

response.snippet: Thank you so much! We love that! Come back!

reviews.snippet: Junzi is great! After a long flight back to New York, I headed straight here for a comforting bowl of beef noodle soup. It hit the spot perfectly—10/10! Staff were very friendly and welcoming and the ambiance was great for unwinding after a long trip.

response.snippet: Good afternoon Sharel, it is great to hear that the first place you went to after a long flight was Junzi! It means so much to us to know that even while people are away from the area they are still thinking about our food! That is probably one of the best compliments we could get! I will be sure to pass your feedback onto my staff as well so they know what a great job the guests feel they are doing! We look forward to the opportunity to serve you again!

reviews.snippet: Tried Ethiopian food for the first time here and was blown away. I was in town and wanted to see the Jazz performance of Julia Danielle (amazing btw highly recommend) and met some friends for a nice, relaxed Sunday evening. We got a mix of sambusas which I highly recommend. They were so good and always brought out fast. The main dishes took more time, but were amazing. We shared a mix of food. The bread was so spongy and perfect for the mix of flavors. Injera is a must while here!

Five stars! This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and Massawa did not disappoint. I ordered the veggie combo and it was so, so good. Everything was flavorful, well seasoned, and such a fun first experience with Ethiopian cuisine. I also tried the sambusas (the little meat pies!) and they were delicious too, a perfect starter. The prices were actually really reasonable, especially for New York. The only thing I’d mention is parking can be tough, but honestly that’s pretty standard for a busy NYC area, so not really a negative. I’d definitely come back. Actually planning my next trip now 😂

Wonderful East African restaurant serving Eritrean & Ethiopian fare. The space and the staff are warm and inviting. I had a hot cup of cinnamon coffee while I waited on the rest of my party to arrive, I recommend it. Laid back cozy vibe, with space to chill while waiting for your table. We had lunch and the prices were great, and the portions generous. We had samplings of the vegan and vegetarian offerings, they offer different levels of spice and their were five in our group with everyone stated and happy. One person in our group also had salmon and attested to its tastiness, it certainly looked like it was prepared perfectly. The injera was light and had the perfect balance of tang - again, ample portions too. Swollen and happy, we had to decline dessert. Overall a wonderful experience. Great for groups, friends, kids, or an intimate date - soooo good!

Very friendly service. Food was delicious with a twist of no utensils. We started with the Sambusa Duo followed by the Fitfit Tebesi and Zegeni with injera. Both delicious with the spicier Zegeni. Great experience.

MASSAWA is an Ethiopian restaurant located in Harlem. It is a casual upscale restaurant, modern and elegant without being pretentious. The food and drinks were amazing! The cocktails were great. We had a MANGOTINI and a BUBBLE GUM MARTINI. For food, we had the vegetable platter which allowed us to try a whole host of things. We added a protein to that , a spicy beef stew. Everyone has a fun tome eating in this unique way. The minor pet peeves I had was that the waitresses didn't explain each dish, and the beautiful and clean toilet had problems flushing. All in all, a very fun, satisfying and unique dining experience.

Stumbled in on a rainy day after a long bus ride and were met with such exquisite hospitality and absolutely delicious food that I had to write a review. Everything is or can be gluten free and the atmosphere is so gorgeous and relaxing. We tried the honey wine on a whim and it’s superb. Marvelous experience, highly recommend to anyone, celiac or not, but being able to order anything off the menu was a particular treat for me.

This was an excellent place to celebrate a special occasion. The staff went above and beyond to ensure we had a wonderful evening. The dishes were prepared with fresh ingredients and presented beautifully. Every flavor was perfectly balanced, and the portions were generous. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone.

The food was absolutely divine! Every dish, from the starter to the entree and the dessert, was simply amazing. It was the best I’ve ever had in the city. You can truly feel the love and passion that went into creating each dish. The atmosphere is incredibly lovely, and the staff is incredibly friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend this place!

One of the best restaurants we’ve been in NYC, very highly recommended. We didn’t have a reservation, but they were able to accommodate our group of 5. The food from starters, to main dish, to dessert were excellent! You can tell that the food was prepared with care and affection. The best way to enjoy their food is to order different things and share with everyone, including their desserts which were hard to pick a favorite. The ambiance is also great, we didn’t have to shout!

After hearing great things about Massawa from a dear friend for years, I decided to give it a shot. Last Friday, the two of us shared a trio of sambusas and an Alitcha Beghe entrée. Everything was delicious! We even had to order another pair of fish sambusas, as that was our favorite of the trio. All of the food is 10/10 though we never received napkins, a must when eating injera with your hands.
Our server was kind and pleasant, but slow and inattentive. She did not give her name, but volunteered her young teen age when we asked for drink recommendations. I received the tasty agave ginger lemonade, instead of the alcohol-based ginger lemonade I ordered. When I did get it, it was pure completely unpalatable. After dinner, we ordered pumpkin lattes with oatmilk. After 20 minutes of waiting, our server returned to tell us that the bartender left to buy oatmilk from a local store and scurried off before we could cancel. It took about 40 minutes to receive lukewarm lattes.
My friend loves this place and wanted to share it with me. The food was wonderful, but the service dampened the experience.

I have been frequenting this restaurant for over 35 years, and it never disappoints. While prices have gotten steeper and portions smaller following renovations that doubled the square footage and lent the previously unassuming space a trendier, more upscale vibe, Massawa remains the best Ethiopian eats in Manhattan. Additionally, the hosts are very gracious, and always ensure patrons—particularly habitues—are treated like family. Insider tip: The owners lived in Naples, Italy, for a long time, so the espresso and coffee drinks are out of this world.

I’ve been to several Ethiopian restaurants before, and this one is great. The menu offers a wide variety of options, including some more unique dishes you don’t often come across, like fish.

I’m a big fan of their slow-cooked chicken; it’s rich, flavorful, and clearly made with care. But what really surprised me was the dessert. I ordered the limoncello sorbet, and it was absolutely to die for. I wasn’t expecting such an explosive burst of flavor… it was refreshing, vibrant, and perfectly balanced.

I already can’t wait to go back just to have it again!

I came here for a Sunday night, dinner and really enjoyed the food. For our first experience of Ethiopian food, I enjoyed the flavors of my salmon dish and the red lentils. Ingera bread was tasty and something different. The Samusa was really good, but I did not care for the sauces. My Agave ginger lemonade drink was ok.

Very delicious Ethiopian food. We were a group of four, including one vegetarian. The very nice server recommended the goat stew and roasted chicken dish, along with the vegan sampler. This allowed us to try many of the top flavors. It was all delicious. Would recommend to all looking to have a fun experience with Ethiopian food.

response.snippet: Thank you so much for coming and sharing your experience! We’re happy to hear you enjoyed our traditional dishes. We truly appreciate your recommendation and look forward to welcoming you and your group again soon! ✨

reviews.snippet:
the restaurant is SO CUTE. would be good for dinner dates. each table has each flowers and the dotted floral decorations to well with the woody feel of the atmosphere. so worth coming by if you’re in the neighborhood.

the food overall was rlly good. i particularly enjoyed the samosa (2 sauces were very flavorful) and the garden salad (the dressing is light and goes perfectly balanced with the watermelon blocks and arugula). the ginger coffee was interesting and very strong.

media.caption: chicken and veggie samosa with sauces, ethiopian blended coffee (asked for additional milk)

reviews.snippet: If you like Ethiopian food this is the place to go. Food is divine. Good cocktails too. Go before 7 for $9 specialty cocktails. The meat and vegetarian combos were both excellent. The Fava bean dip is divine.

The food was delicious!!! So so good. But the service was truly terrible. Maybe it was just the day we went, but multiple tables were getting up to leave after just getting a drink because the service was so slow.

We got drinks after 45 minutes, and they were wrong (and we still got charged). Then, our food came another 30 minutes later and was promptly whisked away because it wasn’t on the GF injera we ordered. The waitress was sassy to us the whole time, which would have been charming and funny if the service wasn’t terrible.

I really hope this spot can figure out the service because the food is 10/10!

Such a lovely place with tasty food! Has an outdoor protected from the wind area and quite large indoor space. We ordered a vegetarian sampler with lamb and salmon and it was way enough for two people. We could not finish the food but it was so good, especially spicy lamb! We also tried a rum cake which was just ok but then i do not have a sweet tooth so perhaps sweet lovers would appreciate it more. I have to say that the menu has many drinks options ranging from mimosas (for those who like festive brunches) to different teas and coffees. I highly recommend this great food stop and will be back myself for sure!

Food 5/5. Everything was flavorful and big portions. The space is nice and good for a date night or a bigger group. -1 star as some of the items on the paper menu were not on the digital ordering menu but our waitress was great and helped remedy.

Nice restaurant, food delicious - the items we ordered were actually similar to (home cooked) Indian - but less spicy - especially the lentil dishes and the Sambusa (similar to an Indian Samosa).

Lovely drinks - especially the Honey wine and the cocktails we ordered were decent too (see the picture of the receipt for the details).

Only feedback would be:

1. The Chicken and Veg Sambusa - we are existing mixed Sambusa (instead of one chicken one and one vegetable one - if we knew we have just ordered the chicken ones.

2. The Veg sampler was delicious but we felt a little pricy for the amount of food.

Very delicious and affordable Ethiopian cuisine.

We went in as a group of 4 for the lunch special and food was delicious. We had the spicy beef and the spicy lamb with collared green, potato stew, cabbage, chickpeas, and red lentils for sharing. You have the option to have individual plate or sharing a plate.

The fermented injera is fluffy like steamed rice cake and with a bit sharp sourness to cut through all the spices to balance the taste.

I think our favorites are spicy beef and chickpea. I ordered ginger coffee, which was quiet unique.

Also an highlight: the rum raisin cake is very very very strong in rum. It is a huge piece soaked in rum and alcohol lingers on the back if the tongue. It is very delicious but I won’t eat it if I needed to work in the afternoon.

Service is a bit slow. You scan QR code for ordering and for paying. Price is very affordable for what you get. It is on the side of Columbia campus and it is one of the best Ethiopian places to eat in the city.
I used to eat here during my Columbia years. Happy to be back. Lots of elbow room to try the food you eat with your hands.

response.snippet: Thank you, Sree, for coming back to Massawa! We’re so glad to welcome you again and honored to be part of your Columbia memories. Thank you for the wonderful pictures, too! We hope to see you again soon 💛

reviews.snippet: Incredible Ethiopian food in a beautiful restaurant. If gluten free make sure to ask for the pure teff injera - soooo good. We had the vegan sampler, ful (fava beans) and spicy lentils, as well as spicy tea, coffee and rum cake. Everything was delicious and enough for 3 people. So many vegan options!

I went to Massawa three times and every time, I had a terrible experience. Food is okay but far cry from some really great Ethiopian places. The worst thing is service – two out of the three times, we had to wait more than one hour to get our food, even though once the restaurant was almost empty and the other time, we saw other groups get their meals ahead of us despite arriving later. The meals are served as the staff wishes to serve it, not as it was ordered – we ordered two veg platters and one portion of meat separately. The food arrived all on one big plate – we didn't ask for it. Some people prefer to have their own plate or don't want to mix their food with meat. On top of this, one time the server added two dishes to the bill worth $40 even though we didn't order them. Eventually they were removed but it took as 20 minutes of arguing and escalating the issue to the manager.

The food was delicious! I would definitely return and recommend a visit to Massawa. My friend had the lamb, my son had the shrimp and I had the salmon. All came with with white rice and a potato dish that consisted of carrots and cabbage. My friend ordered okra with her meal which I sampled and enjoyed. I had chick peas with my dish, it was pureed and spicy by choice. I sampled my son's shrimp and decided if I return I will order that, not that the salmon isn't worth ordering again. The shrimp dish had a somewhat sweetness to it. The restaurant setting is nice and intimate. We ordered just after 3pm and was still within the lunch window. The three meals and two cups of tea cost $61.
Excellent food and service! Highly recommend the veggie platter

response.snippet: Thank you so much for the 5 star review Timaj! We love the picture, too and will repost it ✨ We’re so glad you enjoyed the food and service - and great choice with the veggie platter 🌱😊

reviews.snippet: Massawa is truly a 10/10 in every way ambiance, food and the service the staff here are incredibly kind, welcoming and genuinely passionate about what they do Every visit feels personal, like you’re being taken care of by people who truly want you to have a great experience. I always leave happy and already looking forward to coming back!

I love Ethiopian food and this spot does it great. It can be kind of a trek to get to this Morningside Heights spot if you don't live in the neighborhood, but this place is worth it.

The best way to enjoy your meal here is with shared plates on top of injera bread, which is how Ethiopian food is best eaten. If you're a party of two, I would recommend getting the vegan sampler and pairing it with a meat dish. The tebsi beef is my favorite, but the other options are good too. Pair it with a Habesha Ethiopian beer and you won't be disappointed.
I never tried Ethiopian food until my girl put me on a few weeks ago. This food slaps my taste buds around in so many ways lol. It’s a unique cuisine and I would def recommend trying it.

My friends and I went there for drinks. They have a decent selections of cocktails. We got the African rose, Bellini, and Mangotini which didn’t disappoint. 🥂great service and atmosphere. Plus, you can order and pay on your phone!

I hate that stupid order & pay cube they have, it's like ordering door dash at a restaurant. It turned out to not be mandatory to use it but it took so long for a server to come by that it was unclear what we were supposed to do. Same deal for paying the bill

Good vibes here otherwise but food was kinda just normal

Lunch plate was a great price for a healthy portion of rice (or traditional bread), meat and two sides. The lamb was just right with a bit of spice that added a depth of flavor but was t overwhelming. I would definitely come back to try some of the other items, I was interested in the beef stew as well! Very cute decor and ambience, good for dates as well
Food and atmosphere was great and servers are very kind.

We have decided to quit going here because they stupidly change the amount of food you used to get. Just a joke portion of lentils and a small portion of meat is 28$ dollars. 🙃

I mean are you serious? They also charge you for an extra side at 7$

Dinning here became extremely overpriced. Sorry but not coming here never again!

The experience merits many repeat visits. The five-star limit can't express this quality. Workers here delivered outstanding attention additionally. They provide recently prepared food displayed skillfully. This place has become my favorite and could be yours.

response.snippet: Thank you so much, Lloyd! Your words mean the world to us and we're so happy the experience made such an impression. Our team works hard to create positive and memorable experiences, and knowing we’ve become your favorite place is the highest compliment. We look forward to welcoming you back again and again!

reviews.snippet: Fantastic food. This is my first time enjoying ethiopian food and I have to say, it was worth the wait. I really enjoyed eating with my hands! The protein plate to share was amazing. Definitely coming back.

Wonderful, well-spaced ambience with beautiful Ethiopian food. I was ambitious and had the Ethiopian iced coffee for dinner & did not regret it at all.

We chose all of their sides, and had both the chicken and veggie sambusas as a starter. Heavily recommend either or a combination of the two. Wonderfully lit at night and excellent service near closing time.

The atmosphere is beautiful and the wait staff are very nice. The 3 stars are only for atmosphere and wait staff. I have never had Ethiopian food before and I went here because of the reviews, but the food had no flavor at all. I was prepared to have an explosion of delicious flavors and was extremely disappointed and actually very shocked. It was honestly the most bland food I’ve eaten. The person that came with me had Ethiopian food before and told me she’ll take me some place else for the real experience. I ordered the chicken and she had the lamb.

My meal here left a positive impression. The informal setting and friendly faces make dining pleasant. The workers here really care about good service. My future plans definitely include more visits to Massawa. Best wishes for your dining adventure.

response.snippet: Thank you Do for your kind words! We’re delighted the atmosphere and service made your visit memorable. It means a lot to know Massawa left a lasting impression and we’re happy to have you back again soon ✨

reviews.snippet:
First, do you think this is worth $26 (without tax and tips)? Plus tax is $28.31, and this still doesn’t include tips yet…
Second, maybe they just like to take things slow or they don’t have enough waiters/waitresses, because the wait time is very long. It took me about 20 minutes to order my food and another 20 minutes to see my dishes (totaling around 40 minutes before I can actually eat)!
Third, maybe it’s just me, but that “bread like”thing is really sour.
Fourth, this restaurant is said to be a halal restaurant. However, they do sell alcoholic drinks. So, I don’t think this restaurant can be considered as halal.

Went on a first date here 2 years ago, and now we're married and had our first anniversary dinner here.

Hoping it's open for years to come so we can enjoy more anniversary dinners here.

response.snippet: Scott, this truly means so much to us ✨ Thank you! Being a part of your first date and now your anniversary is incredibly special, and we’re honored to be part of those memories. Wishing you both many more beautiful years together, and we look forward to celebrating many more anniversaries with you! ❤️

reviews.snippet: Excellent Ethiopian food, I found it to be very close to Indian cuisine. The use of spice in the food was good and the Injera (was like dosa) was tasty as well. Good ambience and friendly host. I hear that the restaurant has been there for over 30 years. Good going, that 👍😊
Nice clean place with very convenient ordering and payment through Toast; everything we tried was very good, but a little on a spicy side

media.caption: Zegeni (beef), Alitcha Beghe (lamb) with sides of shiro (split peas) and tsebhi hamli (collard greens)

reviews.snippet: Abraham is a remarkable host. Generous in his hospitality and warmth. The food is exceptional. A must stop every trip. Every offering is a banger! You must go again and again!

The food is bland and very expensive - especially compared to the fantastic alternatives nearby (Awaze and Abyssinia). It tastes like bland gentrified indian food - none of the intense flavourful spices you get elsewhere. Feels inauthentic. I guess it caters to gentrified tastebuds, but is definitely not my thing.

The food was delicious!
we had Silsi Derho, it was really good and Ethiopian coffee was on point. Sambousa was good as well.
I would definitely return and recommend a visit to Massawa.

Poor service, took forever to get water. Food had little to no explanation when served. Had to hunt down our server. Food was great but unfortunately would not return for this poor of service at this price point.
First time trying Ethiopian food and it was delicious. Only downside is that the wait time to receive the food and coffee we ordered was long.
We got the vegetarian sampler and it was great. Not maybe the most amazing Ethiopian food we have but it was good. Service was polite and prompt. Outdoor seating was nice.
Casual but chic ambience. Excellent food. #NYC #Manhattan

response.snippet: Thank you so much Wamuyu for the amazing review and beautiful pictures! 💛 Hope to see you again soon ✨

reviews.snippet: The food is delicious and the restaurant wasn't crowded. It's a really nice spot for lunch, dinner, hanging out with friends, or having a romantic date. It's not often that I come across Eritrean cuisine and I love it.

Craving Ethiopian cuisine or just curious what it looks like? Your spot: Massawa. I especially loved the Vegan sampler which has Injira (bread) along with 4 side dishes: potatoes, lentils, collard greens, and chickpea paste. Delicious! Go for the non-veg sampler if you are craving meat. You will like Ethiopian cuisine so much once you’ve had food at Massawa, you are bound to come again.

We ordered the spicy lamb and the non-spicy chicken to share. The sides and the Injera bread tasted great, and the place had a happy hour. The lady who served us said that the restaurant had been around for 35 years, and I can see why. The place is popular for good reason, and an excellent place to visit and enjoy a good meal.

The food was tasty but there was an issue with our order and we wound up waiting over an hour for our food to come out. I’ll come back because the food was good and hopefully the kitchen issue was just a fluke. I loved the chicken tebsi and wasn’t a huge fan of the salmon.
Wonderful and personal feeling. We got great recommendations from the servers in the 2 times we were there, and they’ve all been great! The split pea really stands out though!

Yummmm
Took the vegan sampler it was delicious. More then enough for 2 hungry people. Best Shiro I’ve had! The soup was also very tasty. Good service will probably come back

BEST ETHIOPIAN FOOD IN NYC!!!
I have tried to find a better place in the city and this one is still my favorite. The food quality is beyond exceptional and the injera has an amazing flavor. Service is incredible as well! Highly recommend!!

Fantastic place with a great outdoor and indoor seating. Great service and the food was good, we had the shrimp, chicken and lamb dishes. The injera is also very fresh and tasty. Don’t miss this gem if in the upper west side.

High quality and incredibly flavorful food. I was particularly impressed with their vegetarian and vegan meals. The freshness of their food was outstanding. It’s always a pleasure coming back to this place.

We ordered all three entrees chicken, lamb, and beef: Tsebhi Beghe, Derho Hiwas, and Zegeni. Among all, beef is my favorite entree, because it is well-cooked and very flavourful. The lamb was a bit undercooked. Great ambiance, perfect for a dinner date.

reviews.snippet:
I celebrated my birthday at The U Bar & Grill recently, and I couldn’t have picked a better spot! From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was perfect—great energy and a really welcoming vibe. The service was top-notch; our server was attentive and made sure the celebration felt special.
As for the food and drinks, everything was amazing! Every dish was flavorful, and the cocktails were expertly crafted. If you’re looking for a place with great food and a fun environment for a special occasion, this is it. I’ll definitely be back!

reviews.snippet:
If you’re looking for a spot to grab drinks and just watch the game, it’s not bad.

Besides that, I’d never recommend anyone to come here. The food is mid, they got our order wrong twice, and it’s pricey for the quality.

reviews.snippet: Tom’s Restaurant was at the top of my bucket list as a Seinfeld fan for 3 decades. The iconic front for Monk’s Diner from the show was everything I wanted it to be and more! The staff were amazing, quick, kind and fun. The coffee was classic, booths were comfy, super cute bar top, and it has an adorable outside patio on a great side of town. Lots of memorabilia from the show and epic photo opportunities for fans. We both ordered BIG Salads and they were fresh and fantastic! Highly recommend for great food and atmosphere. Loved their fries, SO yum! Lots of menu options, yada, yada, yada. 🤣

The chicken cutlet was tasty, but the pasta and sauce had no flavor at all, it honestly tasted like plain crushed tomatoes. I even added some salt and pepper myself, but it didn’t help much. We ordered the steak medium, but it came out well-done.

That said, the atmosphere was nice and the diner itself was beautiful, and all the staff were very kind and friendly.

Came because of Seinfeld and was worried it might be a tourist trap (crowded, overpriced, etc.). I couldn’t have been more wrong. The food was genuinely very good, and the place felt like a true local diner despite its fame. This was actually my second visit. Earlier this year I stopped by for a chicken menu that was also excellent, so it was nice to see that the quality wasn’t a one-off.

The service was excellent, especially from the Hispanic server who looked after us- she was spectacular. My Eggs Benedict were OK, but I tried several dishes from around the table and they were all outstanding. The cheeseburger was particularly delicious.

If you are a fan of classic television, Tom's Restaurant is an absolute must-visit in New York City. This iconic spot is famous for serving as the exterior of the diner in Seinfeld. While the interior doesn't perfectly match the show since those scenes were filmed on a Hollywood soundstage, stepping inside still offers a quintessential, nostalgic American diner experience.

The restaurant is wonderfully decorated with genuine Seinfeld memorabilia, including authentic autographs from the original cast members. Even Jerry Seinfeld himself has visited!

Beyond the incredible pop culture history, the food and service truly stand on their own. The staff, along with the owner, are incredibly welcoming and friendly, making you feel right at home. I highly recommend saving room for dessert because their cheesecake is easily one of the best I have ever had. Additionally, the coffee is surprisingly excellent for a traditional New York diner.

Another major plus is their late-night hours, making it a great spot to grab an evening bite. Beware that the surrounding neighborhood can feel a little unsettled late at night, but that is entirely outside of the business's control. Overall, this is a fantastic establishment that delivers both on its legendary TV status and its high-quality food and service. Highly recommended!

Let’s be real, you’re not coming to Tom’s for the food, you’re coming here because of the show. And while Tom’s certainly caters to the fans by having a number of pictures of the cast, it’s functionally just a typical NYC diner. The Lumberjack was pretty decent

Location known to be iconic from the sitcom Seinfeld. Operates as a diner, but I would say service wise it does not operate as such and you will be rushed to order and eat in order to flip tables. I had the chicken parmigiana sandwich, expensive for the serving size but was alright.

Yummy and lovely diner near Columbia. Everything was very fairly priced and quite delicious. The chocolate chip pancakes in particular stood out and I was very grateful to the continuous refills of coffee. I also love the booth style seating, twas very nostalgic.

media.caption: Diner breakfast eggs pancakes sausage bacon

reviews.snippet:
As a European I was yearning for a great Diner style experience, so what better than to try out the famous Seinfeld joint ? Recommended to me by a New Yorker.
They serve really excellent breakfasts. The poached eggs are marvellous. Great pancakes. Which I covered in maple syrup.
Friendly and efficient service.
I can’t wait to go back tomorrow.

Had dinner at Tom’s, the food was not great. I think paco is cooking again… The corn beef was dry, soup was salty, the Jerry salad w chicken didn’t taste fresh. However! The desert was great. If I ever go back it will be just for the desert. Shakes, ice cream. I went one other time during the day and the food was fine. Might have been just the time of day. The wait staff had some body odor. The place felt like they don’t care. Needs some TLC. Was hoping for the mackinaw peaches, but it wasn’t to be. Next time try a nicer place like Mendy’s.

This place is not a high end resturant but a Clasic American diner.
We went for breakfast wasnt disappointed.
Great spot to take a photo outside if you are a traveling seinfield fan.
I love Seinfeld so I had to go check it out. They have really cool Seinfeld stuff on the walls and it's just got a cool vibe. Is you love Seinfeld it's a must go

You will come because you know it from Seinfeld and you will be delighted to discover that the food is also great. We came during rush hour but got the table immediately. Staff is really friendly, nice and helpful and food is awesome

I absolutely love this restaurant! Everything moves pretty fast, I love Seinfeld and the food is incredibly tasty every time! Some characters work there, but most discrepancies are easily dealt with and are worth the food, 100%. Ive gotten breakfast items and lunch/dinner items and I can never wait to go back. I love an excuse to go to Monk's.... I mean Tom's.. (seinfeld joke.) 10/10, highly recommend.

media.caption: Some of the art on the wall.
Bacon, egg and cheese on a croissant... so good.

reviews.snippet:
Terrible service. We had a server that was rude and on her phone the whole time. Full blow conversations and texting i was in complete disbelief. I had 1 request and i heard her tell the cook she didn't care if i like my food ( my only ask was not to toast my bun) food came out bun was toasted, food was so dry and bland. Low quality meat. How can a diner mess up a cheeseburger deluxe?! Its such a staple for diners... Server Never checked up on us and we went without water the whole meal we had to stop another guy walking not sure his role to ask for the check and water. Major DISSAPOINTMENT we were looking for a new diner in the area we just moved to but this definitely will not be it.
We were two and the check was over 60$.
I dont write many reviews but this was just such a bad experience i have to warn others. If you really wamt to enjoy your food try somewhere ese.

Amazing experience to eat at this world famous diner. There was no wait to get a seat, the staff were very welcoming, attentive and friendly. Happy to answer questions about the origin of the business, asked us where we were from.

The food was really delicious, fast and simple but done well.

Would highly recommend!

reviews.snippet:
I absolutely love little diners and this one did NOT disappoint. The service was great and the food was a lot for the money - and delicious! The connection with the hit TV series added to the enjoyment of eating here. I can’t wait to come back to NYC. I will make this place a regular breakfast stop for me and my family. 😋
Terry from Live Oak, Florida.

Was visiting Columbia for a match and found this place nearby. I didnt know at first that it was famous but wanted a nice diner type meal. It was refreshing to be in a diner with a lot of great brunch options for a reasonable price. I ordered a bacon egg and cheese on a roll and it was delicious for only around $6. The service was fast, even in peak brunch hours. I would definitely come back!

We had breakfast here before Columbia University your. The food is excellent diner food. The service is flawless! But more importantly, the staff and owner are kind hearted people and very welcoming. I imagine they have regulars due to the positive atmosphere. Well done. Btw I had no idea the outside was used for Seinfeld since I didn’t watch show.

Very belated review - Been here many times as a Columbia student, great food and atmosphere for the price. My comment is on a separate incident involving a server: one time in summer of 2025 when I visited with my friends from overseas, the server made the assumption that we wouldn’t tip by *writing* the tip amount on my check, never have I encountered this sort of discriminatory and rude behavior! Management should make clear to their staff this is unacceptable.
Wonderful service. Good and interesting place. Good a little salty but yummy

reviews.snippet:
Stopped by for a quick lunch around 1 PM on a weekday. The place was packed but the line moved surprisingly fast -- kudos to the staff for keeping things running smoothly. I grabbed a booth while waiting for my slices, which was a surprise as the place was filled with kids getting out of school and parents. The ambiance was fun - some good music was playing making lunch break even more enjoyable.

The pizza itself is genuinely good: thin crust, quality cheese, great tomato sauce, and creative toppings. I went with the spicy vodka sauce and the mushroom -- both were delicious.

Price-wise, I paid just over $15 for 2 slices and a Pepsi, which gave me a moment of pause. For the Columbia area though, I get it -- rent around here isn't cheap and that's going to show up in menu prices. It's not an everyday lunch spot for me, but when a real pizza craving hits, I'll definitely be back. The staff was super friendly and efficient, which always makes the experience better.

Solid spot -- just go in knowing it's a treat, not a cheap slice.
Such amazing staff over at Upside Pizza..turned a honest mistake into a wonderful birthday dinner. Such great people who make great pizza. If you haven’t already give them a try!
The spicy vodka pizza had an crispy, firm crust and was quite flavorful. It was $6 for the slice though it was worth trying for the first time. Seating is limited so it might be better to take out.
Such kind staff, and OUTSTANDING pizza !!!! 10/10, will be back again
Visited NYC and got recommended to Upside Pizza…Did not disappoint!! Real taste of NYC pizza

Ordered a pepperoni pizza, it was $40. There was no line, the place is right next to the Seinfeld diner. Got the order, No napkins, no plates, no bag for the soda. This seems like a place you can get a slice and sit. The pizza was ok, too much dough with not much flavor. The sauce was ok also. The lights outside drew me in, but the pizza wasn’t worth the price or the hype. Next time I’ll try across the street for $28.
Casual yet great NYC pizza! The standouts are the Sicilian pepperoni and spicy vodka slices. If you’re passing through the UWS and are craving pizza, stop in and you won’t be disappointed!

The best regular slice on the UWS, as of 3-7-25. Bold? Gurl, it’s my review & you’re just a 🐿️ … Is it the best overall pizza spot though ?

Pros:

It’s an 8.3 One Bite crust crisp factor. Didn’t even need to tell them to cook it well done. Good chew. Thinnest crust.

The cheese is low moisture mozzarella and their topping options are of high quality- Gina.

Pepperoni, mushroom, vodka…basically you can’t go wrong with most…

They deliver & open late.

Cons:

The Detroit style slices are disappointing. Dense and nothing like the real deal, even Jets is better.

They only sell pizza & garlic knots, nothing else. Get your beef Pattie fix across the street, Ricky.

______________________________________

Lots of seating inside for a pizza spot… even more outside, weather permitting.

Friendly staff.

The got Mexican Coke & Fanta. Double Bonus.

It’s a destination. I’d walk from CPW to Broadway for a slice because it beats all other pizza joints in the Morningside/ Columbia hood.

media.caption: The mushroom is legit. The Detroit style is meh. Dough not righty
Their Detroit style is too dense. But decent. 6/10

reviews.snippet: Overall great experience here! The pizza was delicious, very crispy and according to my boyfriend the sourdough crust is to die for (I’m not much of a crust person myself…) We got five slices and it cost $30: cheese, spicy vodka, corn, pepperoni Sicilian, and mushroom slice. The spicy vodka was delicious as was the cheese and pepperoni Sicilian. We were really excited for the corn and mushroom slices but they were a little bit bland, probably because they are white pizza slices. The service was good, we got our food quickly, but the cashier was a little bit brisk with us. Definitely good vibes in the restaurant though, unique flavors, and a fun neighborhood spot. Stop by if you haven’t already!

If you only try one pizza shop in NYC, make it any of Upside Pizza’s locations; and if you try just one slice, make it their Cacio e Pepe slice.

The humble white slice is often overlooked across the city however, I believe any pizza shop need be judged by their basics. If simple slices like their standard cheese or white slice aren’t up to snuff, then what’s the point?

Upside Pizza changed how I view white slices in the city. All of their stuff is great, from the pepperoni used to the crust on all their pies. But the fresh ricotta and shaved parm on the Cacio slice as soon as it leaves the oven? It is truly a *chef’s kiss* moment 🤌 the slice itself is salty, cheesy, dense, garlicky….all without being oily or one-note. It’s a slice that lets the ingredients speak for themselves, much like every pie that Upside makes.

You just can’t beat this place!

I’ve NEVER liked Sicilian pizza. They are too thick and doughy, plain with just sauce and cheese or whatever but upside pizza has it figured out! Their slices are sooo good, it was visually appetizing enough to make me want a slice and I cannot get enough. They’re deep dish pan made like Pizza Hut so the crust is buttery and slightly over cooked. And I don’t know what they put in their sauce but it’s slight my bitter like a vinegar taste that’s just so unique. I’ve put my co-workers on to it too and sometimes we get a box to split. The service is good and quick and they keep the tables clean. The outside ones could use a bit of care but people should wipe the tables behind themselves as well.

media.caption: Pepperoni pizza slice on checkered paper

reviews.snippet: Tried the pizza because the restaurant always smelled really good whenever I passed. The pizza was good, especially the crust, but too salty in my opinion. Service is quick, and there is plenty of seating. Overall, a convenient option, but I wasn't amazed.
Upside Pizza is a life savior for a true New York meal after a long day. The staff os very nice and the pizza is really really good for a very reasonable price.
Very diverse assortment of slices! Theyre all well made on a nice dough. I recommend the spicy vodka slice. The staff is also very polite!

Drove in from Chicago and decided to check out the famous Seinfeld restaurant. Right across the street, we noticed this busy pizza spot—the amazing aroma instantly caught our attention. The staff were incredibly welcoming, and honestly, all those 5-star reviews don’t do it justice. The pizza was thin with a perfect crispy crunch on the bottom. This spot truly completed our New York experience!
Great pizza! Especially loved the cacio e peppe, spicy vodka, and mushroom. Sour dough crust is a bonus

Will probably give it another shot, but slice was tiny, and kind of burnt. The pepperoni were salty and nicely crisped up but didn’t taste of much - more like little cups of spam. The slice was edible but nothing compared to Sal and Carmines or Mama’s Too.

Five bucks for this slice was a bit of head fake.

Used to go to their soho location at least once a week. Hyped that they opened one near campus. And the quality is exactly as good (dare i say better?) than what i expected from their shop in soho. Best pizza in neighborhood hands down! Well… Mama’s Too is on a similar level but who’s got time to walk that far?
Spicy vodka and sausage pizza were fantastic! Thin crispy crust, sauce had a lot of flavor. Pittsburgh natives, we were impressed! Tom's restaurant from Seinfeld across the street!
The Neopolitan style better than Sicilian ( although Sicilian looked more appealing). Welcoming, efficient, family feeling.

The food is definitely a bit over priced for what you get though. I got the tacos and it didn’t even come with a side of rice and beans, that was separate and it wasn’t very filling. Other folks got the nachos which seemed to be good. The drinks were also okay, the margaritas are delicious. If you go with a large party be mindful that they are only willing to accept 3 cards which was pretty annoying.

We're glad to know, though, that you liked how you were immediately attended to and that you loved the nachos and margaritas. We hope you give us another try. Please check out the rest of our menu here: https://theheightsnyc.com/food-drinks/. We hope to serve you soon!

reviews.snippet:
10/10 so good. Jake was an AMAZING servicer. Loved the chips & guac app, we got yummy mini margaritas, I got the chicken burrito (mind blowingly good) and my friend got the burger. So delicious.

One thing to note, they have rooftop seating but it might not be what you expect. The walls are higher, so you don’t really have a great view. But it was still nice to be outside

The food was delicious!! It was cool going up the heights! It feels like a cozy place. It was almost closing time when we went so it was on the quiet side and I enjoyed the atmosphere. I like it was on the darker side and feels like we had privacy and our waitress was nice and friendly! Didn’t get any drinks but the bar looked awesome!
Burger was just ok, wouldn't order again for the price. Room temperature was a bit cold.

Food was great especially the nachos and Mexican Cobb Salad. Unfortunately we were denied a table for two by the window despite several subsequent pairs of people being allowed in the same seats we requested.

I will never go back here. I got very sick while sitting in this establishment shortly after eating. Not only did I faint but I threw up and there was not one single person in the staff that was attentive and no action was taken to assure I was feeling ok or if the food I was served was bad.

reviews.snippet: The braised short rib was cooked great ! Nice and smooth not dry at all ! Frozen drinks were great amazing as well ❤️

The Heights is unassuming chic at its best. Not quite a rooftop, but it's on the upper level of a third storey walk. Above average customer service with a sensual southern atmosphere. Great dive for a dirty night. Very dark and discrete. Screams Tinder.

Small place that gets crowded quickly. Food is always great. Mostly been for brunch. Last time I was there the bathroom was really gross a bunch of flies like a lot that concern me the bathroom is pretty close to the kitchen and bar. The big huge windows can be open and have no screen. No insect traps I could see. The wait staff is great kind friendly and accommodating.

I was walking and by accident I stumbled into this amazing hidden gem. Friday 1:37pm and these guys are amazing. I love this place!!!

Great little joint with a lot of stairs. There’s a rooftop but there’s also food. The food also can come with drinks. The drinks can also come with a variety of appetizers. And believe it or not the appetizers can even come with a variety of entrees. A true restaurant. Oh and it a Columbia venue cause it’s next to Columbia, give it take 6 blocks.

Everything about the Heights is great except for management. I never feel “welcomed” when I’m there
Nice place if u want to drink a draft beer or a nice froz Margarita! Happy Hour until 11pm! And a nice college pub like atmosphere! Rooftop is also nice!

reviews.snippet:
This is no ordinary street cart! They have a wide selection of gourmet breakfast offerings using top quality ingredients. I’ve had the Mediterranean Pita Pocket and the French Toast. Both were delicious. The Feta cheese they use in the sandwiches is literally the best I’ve ever had. Maybe the outdoor setting enhances the flavors!

They also have a real espresso machine and make a full range of delicious espresso drinks. I got a Freddo Cappuccino made in the authentic Greek style. They also carry premium Pellegrino sodas.

Prices are very reasonable for this level of quality.

It’s very unusual to find a specialty food cart at a location like this on quiet Morningside Drive. Cafe Valona certainly deserves our support. Sit back on a park bench and enjoy!

response.snippet: Thank you for your wonderful review! We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed our Mediterranean Pita Pocket and French Toast, and we're glad you appreciated the quality of our ingredients. It's great to know that the Freddo Cappuccino hit the mark for you, too! We strive to create a unique experience for our customers, and your support means a lot to us. We hope to see you again soon to enjoy more of what Cafe Valona has to offer!
